summary: Iteration 19 — validated the switch from simulated seller orders to real db.orders and the new bulk tracking flow. 6/6 backend pytest tests pass on live URL; full frontend E2E (login → 46 real orders visible → bulk update 2 orders to 'Expédié de Chine' → toast + persistence after refresh → cleanup back to 'Commandé' → dashboard has no fake trend badges → 15s idle produces no fake simulated orders → public menu shows 'Électronique' and '10-20 jours' everywhere → /suivi/ord_demo12345678 still shows 'En douane') all passed. Demo order preserved. Tracking ETA = created_at + 10 days verified.

issues: Recharts console warnings: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' — non-blocking, chart container has no min height at first render. Suggest adding minHeight to ResponsiveContainer parents.

action_items: Optional: silence Recharts sizing warnings by giving ResponsiveContainer parents an explicit min-height (256/160 as the warning suggests).
critical_code_review_comments: orders_router.py cleanly uses request.app.state.db + get_current_seller — good; MongoDB _id is excluded from the projection (no ObjectId leaking).
bulk-tracking uses update_many with $push tracking_history — correct, but has no per-order 'before/after' record; acceptable for MVP.
get_current_seller reads cookie first then Bearer — matches the auth playbook (httpOnly cookie + Authorization fallback).
SellerContext polls every 30s — reasonable, but consider a manual refresh button to avoid rate pressure.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing 46 real orders in db.orders; bulk-changed 2 to 'shipped' then restored to their original 'ordered' via PUT /api/tracking/{id}. ord_demo12345678 was NOT touched.
